proposals.before: In the first month of Hailing's Zhenglong 4 (1159), the court closed the markets at Fengxiang Prefecture and at Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and Jiaoxi County, concentrating border trade at Sizhou alone.
proposals.after: In the first month of Hailing's Zhenglong 4 (1159), the court closed the markets at Fengxiang Prefecture and at Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and other prefectures, as well as Jiaoxi County, concentrating border trade at Sizhou alone.
proposals.reason: Chinese lists 唐、鄧、潁、蔡、鞏、洮等州 (Tang, Deng, Ying, Cai, Gong, Tao, and other prefectures); idiomatic omits 等 ('and others').

proposals.before: In the tenth month of Xuanzong's Zhenyou 3 (1215) Gao Rulü was sent to buy grain in Henan and require transport to the capital; capital granaries were also to buy any surplus the people still held.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of Xuanzong's Zhenyou 3 (1215) Gao Ruli was sent to buy grain in Henan and require transport to the capital; capital granaries were also to buy any surplus the people still held.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'Gao Rulü' conflicts with 'Gao Ruli' in s0098 for the same 高汝礪; standardize to Gao Ruli.

proposals.before: In the first month of year five an edict ordered plot farming; memorialist Wu Zhi Gao Yi had earlier submitted the method and asked to set planting quotas based on household registers and land holdings.
proposals.after: In the first month of year five an edict ordered plot farming; memorialist Gao Yi of Wuzhi had earlier submitted the method and asked to set planting quotas based on household registers and land holdings.
proposals.reason: 武陟 is the place Wuzhi, not part of the personal name; 高翌 is Gao Yi.

proposals.before: In the first month of the fifth year an edict instructed farmers to use plot farming; earlier, memorialist Wu Zhi Gao Yi submitted the plot-farming method and also requested verifying household registers and land holdings, fixing quotas for planting.
proposals.after: In the first month of the fifth year an edict instructed farmers to use plot farming; earlier, memorialist Gao Yi of Wuzhi submitted the plot-farming method and also requested verifying household registers and land holdings, fixing quotas for planting.
proposals.reason: Same place/name fusion: 武陟高翌 is Gao Yi of Wuzhi.

proposals.before: The original three-month-per-capita target risked spoilage and was replaced by tiered quotas: 30,000 shi for counties above 20,000 households, 20,000 for above 10,000, 15,000 for 5,000–10,000, and 5,000 for below 5,000.
proposals.after: The original plan to store three months' grain by household register risked spoilage from large quantities and was replaced by tiered quotas: 30,000 shi for places above 20,000 households, 20,000 for above 10,000, 15,000 for 5,000–10,000, and 5,000 for below 5,000.
proposals.reason: Chinese 舊擬備戶口三月之糧 refers to storing by household-register population, not clearly 'per capita' alone; and 改令戶二萬以上 is jurisdiction household-count tiers.

proposals.before: Officials who induced 5,000 shi or more had one review grade reduced; 10,000 shi brought one promotion and two grades reduced; 20,000 shi one promotion and one grade raised—all to current vacancies.
proposals.after: Investigation and county officials who induced 5,000 shi or more had one review grade reduced; 10,000 shi brought one promotion and two grades reduced; 20,000 shi one promotion and one grade raised—all to current vacancies.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司縣官 specifies investigation and county officials; the idiomatic English drops that qualification.

proposals.before: In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 2, on Daxing Prefecture Administrator Xu Ding's request, provisional favor-sale rates were fixed for rank advancement, mourning candidates seeking office, manumission of registered households, and similar benefits, each with set grain or fodder payments.
proposals.after: In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 2, on Daxing Prefecture Administrator Xu Ding's request, provisional favor-sale rates were fixed for advancement in palace rank and promotion, permission for those in mourning to take examinations and seek office, manumission of registered households, and similar benefits, each with set grain or fodder payments.
proposals.reason: Chinese 進宮升職 and 丁憂人許應舉求仕 are more specific than the idiomatic 'rank advancement' and 'mourning candidates seeking office'.

decisions.reason: s0005 has 唐、鄧、潁、蔡、鞏、洮等州並膠西縣; the idiomatic drops 等 and collapses the prefecture list into Jiaoxi County. Restoring "and other prefectures, as well as Jiaoxi County" matches the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐、鄧、潁、蔡、鞏、洮等州並膠西縣

decisions.reason: s0097 and s0098 name the same person 高汝礪; 礪 is lì, and s0098 already has Gao Ruli. Idiomatic Gao Rulü is a wrong romanization, not a distinct alias.
s0204 has 陳言人武陟高翌: 武陟 is the place Wuzhi and 高翌 is the personal name Gao Yi. Treating "Wu Zhi Gao Yi" as a fused personal name is wrong; "Gao Yi of Wuzhi" is accurate.
Same source phrase 武陟高翌 on the literal field: Wuzhi is the place qualifier, Gao Yi the name. The proposed "Gao Yi of Wuzhi" corrects the fusion.

decisions.after: The original plan to store three months' grain by household register risked spoilage from large quantities and was replaced by tiered quotas: 30,000 shi for counties above 20,000 households, 20,000 for above 10,000, 15,000 for 5,000–10,000, and 5,000 for below 5,000.
decisions.reason: s0148 舊擬備戶口三月之糧，恐數多致損 is not well rendered by "three-month-per-capita target risked spoilage"; restore household-register storage and spoilage from large quantities. But surrounding units fix county granaries, so keep "counties" rather than the proposal's vaguer "places".

sourceWitness.excerpt: 舊擬備戶口三月之糧，恐數多致損，改令戶二萬以上備三萬石

decisions.reason: s0232 specifies 司縣官, and s0231 already renders the same office class as "Investigation and county officials"; bare "Officials" drops that qualification.
s0226 lists 進宮升職 and 丁憂人許應舉求仕; "rank advancement" and "mourning candidates seeking office" omit palace-rank/promotion pairing and the explicit permission to sit examinations (應舉).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 進宮升職、丁憂人許應舉求仕

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0002 shows Gao Rulü was only a bad romanization of 高汝礪 in s0097; the correct personal name Gao Ruli remains in c0075/c0077, so this alternate-name claim has no independent source support.

Accepting r0003 shows 武陟 is the native place and 高翌 the personal name; the fused alternate-name "Wu Zhi Gao Yi" was created solely by the bad translation. Native-place Wuzhi remains in c0342 and personal name Gao Yi in c0158.
